reviews.reason: The configured whitespace policy intentionally ignores trailing blank lines. This is not an incorrect solution.
A monotone stack may retain equal heights; popping them later still measures the complete plateau. Both > and >= variants are valid.
The variant has signed-overflow portability risk, but the final int32 comparison can still agree under the current compiler. Its tag is not a demonstrated wrong-output witness.
N <= 2e9; the largest tested square is 44723^2 = 2000190729, below INT_MAX. The claimed int32 overflow cannot occur within the specified range.
The subsequent (s+2)^2 <= N loop restores an exact odd-square boundary. The changed first comparison does not change the final ring.
Signed overflow is nonportable, but the power-of-two modulus and final normalization preserve low bits with this compiler. No valid wrong-output witness has been established.
The complete backtracking search is logically valid. Slower code that finishes within the time budget must be accepted; worst-case performance remains a separate audit.
Synchronized iostreams are still semantically correct. The judge cannot require a particular I/O library; stress calibration remains a separate gate.
Discovered names can be fewer than the declared population P. This candidate omits unnamed isolated people and is not a correct reference.
The FIFO implementation re-enqueues every improved distance until convergence. It is a label-correcting shortest-path algorithm, not one-pass BFS.
The target still returns at cnt[target] == k. Allowing one extra expansion elsewhere does not shift the kth distance with nonnegative edge weights.
Although it does not exit BFS early for equal endpoints, prev[start] is already -1, so final reconstruction still emits the valid one-word path.
The candidate fails to reserve a seat for the guide. The original first hidden expected answer was also wrong; the guarded correction restores ceil(20/(5-1))=5.
Independent of unresolved parallel-road semantics, this candidate also omits the guide seat and fails valid unambiguous inputs.
Land is the character at the king's starting location; the statement permits any two map letters. This candidate incorrectly hardcodes l.

The original statement permits positive integer constants only. This historical reference incorrectly returns 0 for the standalone zero literal instead of illegal. The new legal syntax-validation case demonstrates WA while all four archived cases remain AC. Preserve the exact historical source as a known rejection, not a retired candidate; the independently verified Python official solution enforces positivity and handles unbounded intermediate integers.

The historical BFS hard-caps program length at300, although legal m=1 inputs can require999999999 additions. Its captured output incorrectly labels that legal case impossible, and a following legal large case throws std::bad_alloc in the isolated64MiB judge. The original sample remains AC.
